description:
FILED s409 (Fable review of s408).  #368 (s408, 49b8a0c) made `__SUB__` inside an
ANONYMOUS sub DIE (rule 12: its no-op lambda flowed into arithmetic, printing 0
where perl prints 120).  The die is right by the s329 boundary -- but the
review's companion run found its cost, which s408 did not measure (only
op/current_sub.t was re-run after #368):

    op/sub.t  51/14 -> 25/6  DIFF   crash: PCL: __SUB__ inside an anonymous sub
                                    is not supported          (both runs agree)

op/sub.t:214 -- `sub { local $depth = $depth + 1; ...; CORE::__SUB__->() }->()`,
the [perl #122845] closure-recursion test -- aborts the file: 26 passing rows
lost.  Snapshot row edited by hand (docs/perl-suite-run.tsv, s409 note).

And the shape MATTERS: `__SUB__` in an anon sub is THE modern-Perl spelling of a
recursive closure (5.16+, `use feature "current_sub"`); a NAMED sub can just
call itself by name, so the anon case is the one real code writes:

    my $fact = sub { $_[0] <= 1 ? 1 : $_[0] * __SUB__->($_[0] - 1) };   # perl 120

FIX SHAPE -- a SOURCE-LEVEL self-reference rewrite at the ONE PPI entry that
already rewrites a NAMED sub's `__SUB__` to `\&name` (find it: grep __SUB__ in
Pl/Parser*.pm).  For an ANON sub whose body (excluding nested subs) mentions
`__SUB__`:

    sub { BODY }   ==>   do { my $__SUB__N; $__SUB__N = sub { BODY[__SUB__ -> $__SUB__N] }; $__SUB__N }

one fresh N per anon sub, innermost-enclosing wins for nested anon subs (the same
"latest start covers" rule #337 uses).  `my $walk; $walk = sub { $walk->() }` is
a shape PCL already compiles correctly (closure over a file/block lexical), so
this rides an existing path with zero new mechanism -- and zero cost for anon
subs that do not mention `__SUB__`.  Alternative rejected: a dynamic
`*pcl-current-sub*` bound per anon call (a special bind on EVERY anon-sub call
to serve a rare token).

Watch: (1) `__SUB__` must be the SAME reference as the enclosing coderef
(`__SUB__ == $f` true in perl); the rewrite gives exactly that.  (2) The `do {}`
wrapper in expression position -- `sub {...}->()`, `\&{sub {...}}`, `map { sub
{...} } ...`, a hash value, a return value; probe each vs perl.  (3) Inside a
NAMED sub, `__SUB__` stays `\&name` (already right).  (4) `CORE::__SUB__`
spelling.  (5) An anon sub inside a `my sub` (#337 rename) -- the rename runs
first; the token is a Word `__SUB__`, unaffected.

BAR: op/sub.t back to >= 51/14 and op/current_sub.t measured (it never reached
the stub -- see what it reaches now); the guard rows in Pl/t/misc-fixes-02.t
flip from "dies" to the perl value (probe 5 shapes: factorial, fib via two
levels of nesting, `__SUB__ == $f`, `sub {...}->(3)`, `CORE::__SUB__`);
corpus-diff (which files carry anon __SUB__ -- explain each); the drop
census; sweep TOTAL/LOST (a Parser change).  Delete the #368 not-supported.md
paragraph in the same commit.

Related: #368 (done, the die), #337 (the rename that must run first).


DONE s410 (`abdeedd`).  Implemented as ruled.  Two things the work turned
up: PPI OVERLOADS STRINGIFICATION to an element CONTENT (so a hash keyed by
a PPI object is keyed by TEXT -- it collides and goes stale; keyed by
refaddr now), and the pass had to move to LAST in _ppi_parse chain because
an ANON sub signature is one Token::Prototype until _desugar_anon_signatures
runs.  op/sub.t 25/6 -> 52/13, one row BETTER than the 51/14 before #368
(the [perl #122845] row now passes; the old no-op lambda never recursed).
Its bar also needed the `our` tail fix (`03cc639`, task #380 half): with a
real recursion, `our $ok++, return if $depth == 2` had to work.
Drop census t/op/current_sub.t 4 -> 3.  17 shapes probed vs perl.
subject: IMPLEMENT anon `__SUB__` (self-reference rewrite: `do { my $__SUB__N; $__SUB__N = sub { … $__SUB__N … }; $__SUB__N }`) -- #368's die costs op/sub.t 26 rows (51/14 -> 25/6, found by the s409 companion) and the shape is modern Perl's recursive closure
